  <Icon data={primary} altData={alternative} showAlt={true} />
)
```

Note: For a whole icon set, register it in sources and select icons by name or altName instead of passing the set alongside a name prop.

#### Follow application state

Bind showAlt to your framework’s boolean state. When using names, keep them explicit so the Vite plugin can collect both drawings.

#### An alternative is not a fallback

Alternative selection is intentional, not an error recovery mechanism. If the active drawing cannot load, use fallback content or handle the loading state. The adapter does not invent a filled counterpart.

chapters.title: Global Styling
Astro overview
chapters.markdown:
### Astro overview

[Source](/guide/astro/overview)

The same icon vocabulary, with an API that belongs in your Astro application.

#### Start with one icon

Use the exact set:name identifier from the catalog. The name selects the artwork; the remaining props control its presentation.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={24}
  color="#7712f7"
/>
```

- [Follow the first-icon tutorial](/guide/astro/getting-started)

#### A shared set of props

Start with a name or inline data, then add only the props you need. Omitted values inherit the application’s defaults.

| Prop | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| name | The exact set:name identifier of the primary icon |
| data | Inline primary icon data; takes priority over name |
| altName | The exact name of an alternative icon; no suffix is inferred |
| altData | Inline alternative icon data; takes priority over altName |
| showAlt | true selects the alternative group; false keeps the primary group |
| size | A named size preset, pixel value or CSS length |
| color | CSS color used by currentColor in the SVG |
| strokeWidth | Outline weight on a 24-unit basis |
| rotate | Rotation in quarter turns: 1 = 90° |

Note: Choose one source per group: name or data for the primary icon, altName or altData for the alternative. Providing both in either group logs console.error; data or altData still takes priority, even if that group is not currently shown.

- [Compare prop support and Vite modes](/guide/rendering)

#### Rendering and loading

Astro renders on the server and waits for asynchronous icon data. Use local data or static extraction for offline output. Remote fetches need an absolute URL; the icon itself does not need a client:* directive.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.markdown:
### Getting started

[Source](/guide/astro/getting-started)

Display one Astro icon, check that it works, then change its appearance. No shared configuration is needed yet.

Before you start: Start with an existing Astro application. Run the commands from its root directory.

Outcome: A visible star icon that you can resize and recolor with a single prop.

#### 1. Install the packages

The adapter renders SVGs. The Vite plugin finds literal icon names in your code and includes their artwork in your build.

Run these commands inside your application.

File: Terminal

```
bun add @icones/astro
bun add -d @icones/vite
```

Run these commands in your application directory. They require access to the @icones packages in your registry; if a package is unavailable, obtain a compatible release before continuing.

Check your result: Your app has both @icones/astro and @icones/vite in its dependencies.

#### 2. Connect the artwork

Add icones to your existing plugin list; keep your framework’s other plugins. Set dataDir to the directory containing your icon JSON files. This example assumes icons is inside the application root.

On the Icons page, find tabler:star, open its JSON tab and save the original JSON as icons/tabler/data/star.json in your application. Keep the collection’s license from the Licenses page with any artwork you use.

In Astro, update vite.plugins in astro.config.mjs. Do not create a separate Vite config.

File: astro.config.mjs

```
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config"
import { icones } from "@icones/vite"

export default defineConfig({
  vite: {
    plugins: [icones({
      mode: "symbol",
      dataDir: "./icons",
      emitData: false,
    })],
  },
})
```

File: project-layout.txt

```
your-app/
  icons/tabler/data/star.json
  astro.config.mjs
```

Note: Use the original tuple JSON from the JSON tab, not SVG markup. Save other icons with the same <set>/data/<name>.json layout. Set fallbackToApi: false to prevent build-time requests for missing icons.

Check your result: The file icons/tabler/data/star.json exists in your application. dataDir points to ./icons, the folder containing tabler/, not to the JSON file itself.

- [Vite and API loading](/guide/loading)

#### 3. Display your first icon

Put this example in your IconExample.astro component and render that component in your page. The literal name tabler:star matches the artwork from step 2.

Run your app with its normal development command and open the page. Verify the star is visible before continuing.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={24}
/>
```

Check your result: You see one 24px star. In the DOM it contains an SVG; no IconConfig or runtime API setup is required.

#### 4. Change one thing at a time

In the previous example, change size from 24 to 32. Once the star grows, add color to make it purple. Keep the name and loading setup unchanged.

This complete replacement example combines those two changes. Remove color to follow the surrounding text color again.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={32}
  color="#7712f7"
/>
```

Check your result: The same star is now 32px and purple. You changed its presentation, not its source JSON.

- [Next: color, sizing and stroke](/guide/astro/color)
- [Later: share defaults with IconConfig](/guide/astro/icon-config)

#### If the icon does not appear

Check these in order before adding configuration. Shared defaults cannot fix a missing import, an incorrect path or missing artwork.

Reference section (optional).

- Check the terminal for a missing-package or missing-icon error.
- Confirm the icon’s name is exactly tabler:star, and dataDir contains tabler/data/star.json.
- Restart the development server after changing its configuration.
- Confirm your page actually renders the component containing Icon.
- Check that CSS is not hiding the SVG or giving it the same color as the background.
- Use a literal name for this lesson. Computed names need local data or a runtime loading setup; learn that after the first icon works.

chapters.title: Color
chapters.markdown:
### Color

[Source](/guide/astro/color)

Let icons follow your text, or give a single icon its own color.

#### Inherit text color

Monochrome icons use currentColor. When color is omitted, the drawing follows the surrounding text color, so it fits naturally inside links, buttons and status messages.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={24}
/>
```

#### Set an explicit color

The color option accepts a CSS color. Use a hex value, a named color, or a design token such as var(--accent-color).

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  color="#7712f7"
  size={24}
/>
```

#### Color in Outline, Filled and Solid icons

The SVG color value does not replace every fill or stroke. It affects only paint values that use currentColor. The artwork decides whether that color appears on an outline or a filled area.

Outline, Filled and Solid describe the artwork, not color modes. Select the exact icon name to change styles; setting color or fill does not turn an outline drawing into its designed filled counterpart.

| Style | What changes with color |
| --- | --- |
| Outline | Usually colors strokes (stroke="currentColor") while fill="none" keeps the center empty. Example: tabler:star. |
| Filled | Usually colors the solid shape through fill="currentColor". Example: tabler:star-filled. It does not add a separate outline. |
| Solid | The same color behavior as Filled, with the collection’s own naming. Example: bootstrap:star-fill. |

Note: Judge by the SVG paint values, not just the style label. For example, bootstrap:star draws a hollow outline with a filled path, while the bundled phosphor:star uses a currentColor stroke.

- [Collection differences](/guide/collections)

#### Respect multicolor artwork

A drawing with fixed fill or stroke colors keeps those colors. currentColor only affects paths designed to inherit it; it does not recolor every path in a flag or brand mark.

chapters.title: Sizing
chapters.markdown:
### Sizing

[Source](/guide/astro/sizing)

Use a shared size preset, a pixel value, or a CSS length.

#### Named presets

The built-in presets cover common interface sizes. Your application can override its defaults.

| xs | sm | md | lg | xl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12px | 16px | 20px | 24px | 28px |

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="lg"
/>
```

#### Pixels and CSS lengths

A numeric size is measured in pixels. A CSS length, such as 1.5rem or 1em, lets the icon follow your type scale. It controls both dimensions.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="1.5rem"
/>
```

#### Canvas versus display size

The original viewBox describes the drawing’s coordinates, not its rendered pixel size. A 24 × 24 drawing can be displayed at 64px without rewriting the source data.

To set separate width and height values, omit size. An explicit size takes priority over both.

chapters.title: Stroke Width
chapters.markdown:
### Stroke Width

[Source](/guide/astro/stroke-width)

Adjust icons drawn with SVG strokes. Filled paths keep their original shape.

#### Set the outline weight

strokeWidth uses a normalized 24-unit basis. This makes the same value usable across collections with different source canvas dimensions.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={32}
  strokeWidth={1.5}
/>
```

#### Keep a constant pixel weight

Set absoluteStrokeWidth with a numeric pixel size to keep the stroke’s rendered thickness steady as the icon gets larger.

This calculation uses the resolved width and height, not a browser layout measurement. Numeric pixels and px strings work; relative CSS units or a later CSS size override do not guarantee a fixed pixel stroke.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size={48}
  strokeWidth={2}
  absoluteStrokeWidth={true}
/>
```

#### Preserve the original drawing

Filled artwork does not gain an outline just because strokeWidth is set. The configured width takes priority over the source width.

Multicolor artwork with fixed stroke colors is excluded from automatic path stroke rewriting.

An Outline label does not guarantee editable strokes: bootstrap:star is a filled path. Phosphor Regular uses strokes that respond to strokeWidth, while Phosphor Fill uses filled shapes that keep their geometry.

Omitting strokeWidth still uses the shared default of 1.5, in both svg and symbol modes. Component props accept a numeric width; there is no cross-framework strokeWidth="original" value. Set an explicit weight when you need a thinner or bolder drawing.

- [Prop support](/guide/prop-support)

chapters.title: Fill
chapters.markdown:
### Fill

[Source](/guide/astro/fill)

Choose artwork intentionally: outline and filled icons are independent drawings.

#### Choose the filled drawing

Use the exact filled icon name from the collection. For example, tabler:star and tabler:star-filled are two different icons.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star-filled"
  size={24}
  color="#7712f7"
/>
```

#### Understand SVG fill

The fill attribute is inherited by paths that do not set their own fill. It does not replace a path’s explicit fill="none", and it cannot turn an outline into a carefully designed filled variant.

For custom tuple data, specify fill in the artwork. Inline rendering can supply a missing fill from the prop, but generated symbols bake missing root fills as none; the root SVG fill prop cannot override that explicit value.

Note: Do not guess a -filled name. Some collections use different names, or do not include a corresponding filled drawing.

- [Collection differences](/guide/collections)

#### Switch between variants

Use altName and showAlt when an icon has two known states. The Alternative guide explains explicit variant selection.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  altName="tabler:star-filled"
  showAlt={true}
  size={24}
/>
```

chapters.title: IconConfig
chapters.markdown:
### IconConfig [Source](/guide/astro/icon-config) Set shared defaults for your icons, customize their appearance, then choose local sources, an API or a shared store. #### Basic usage Configuration is optional. Without custom settings, icons use the built-in md size (20px) and a stroke width of 1.5. Add shared configuration when several icons should use the same defaults. Consider an article toolbar: its main actions need 24px icons, while a compact action needs a 16px icon. Set the common value once, then override only the exception. The example demonstrates icon configuration; connect the buttons to your own application actions. Create one scope with createIconConfig and pass it to all three icons. The first two inherit defaultSize: 24; the last supplies size: 16. Astro uses explicit scopes rather than a provider component: surrounding HTML does not pass configuration to descendants. - Reuse the same scope for icons that should share defaults. Creating a scope does not change unrelated icons elsewhere on the page. - defaultSize belongs to shared configuration; size belongs to one icon. Removing the explicit size makes that icon inherit the shared value again. - Button text supplies the accessible name; the icons remain decorative. Configuration affects Icones icons, not arbitrary SVG elements or the button’s CSS layout. File: IconConfigExample.astro ``` --- import { Icon, createIconConfig } from "@icones/astro" const scope = createIconConfig({ defaultSize: 24 }) ---
``` Note: Keep your existing loading setup. With Vite, include tabler/data/star.json and tabler/data/heart.json in dataDir for these examples. Shared appearance settings do not load artwork. Check your result: The first two buttons contain 24 × 24 icons, and the compact action contains a 16 × 16 icon. Change defaultSize to 20: only the first two change; the explicit 16px override stays the same. - [First, display an icon](/guide/astro/getting-started) #### Customize appearance Use sizeValues to customize named size presets, defaultSize to choose a shared size or a size for each set, and strokeWidth to set the outline weight. Omitted settings keep their inherited defaults. In this example, Tabler uses lg at 28px and a fixed 2px stroke; other sets use md at 20px and a normalized stroke width of 1.5. The heart uses an explicit size of 32, overriding its set’s default size. defaultSize, sizeValues, strokeWidth and absoluteStrokeWidth accept shared values or maps keyed by set. Use default for unmatched sets. For sizeValues, each set contains its own preset dictionary; missing presets fall back to default, then the built-in values. The original flat form, such as sizeValues: { lg: 28 }, still works for shared presets. - Use named sizes such as sm and lg as design tokens. Change sizeValues once to update all icons using that preset; a numeric size such as 32 does not use the preset dictionary. - A normalized strokeWidth of 1.5 renders at 1.5px on a 24px icon and scales with its size. absoluteStrokeWidth keeps the rendered stroke fixed when the icon has a numeric pixel size; it does not change filled artwork. - Keep color on the icon or inherit it from CSS currentColor. IconConfig has no shared color or fill option. A per-icon strokeWidth or absoluteStrokeWidth overrides the corresponding scope setting. | Icon in this example | Resolved size | Rendered stroke | | --- | --- | --- | | tabler:star | 28px — Tabler’s lg preset | 2px — fixed | | lucide:star | 20px — default md preset | 1.25px — 1.5 × 20 / 24 | | tabler:heart | 32px — explicit size | 2px — fixed | File: IconConfigExample.astro ``` --- import { Icon, createIconConfig, type IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" const config = { defaultSize: { tabler: "lg", default: "md" }, sizeValues: { tabler: { lg: 28 }, default: { xl: 32 } }, strokeWidth: { tabler: 2, default: 1.5 }, absoluteStrokeWidth: { tabler: true, default: false }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions const scope = createIconConfig(config) --- ``` Note: The Tabler star is 28px, the Lucide star is 20px and the heart is 32px. With Vite, also add lucide/data/star.json to dataDir. strokeWidth affects SVG strokes, not outlines drawn with filled paths. #### Configuration inheritance Use a child configuration when one part of the interface needs different defaults. Here the page uses 24px icons and the toolbar uses 16px. These examples are independent of the custom presets above. Create a child scope by passing the original scope as the second argument. Pass toolbarScope to the toolbar icon and keep scope on the page icon. | Child defaultSize | With parent { tabler: 28, default: 20 } | | --- | --- | | Not set | Tabler: 28px; other sets: 20px | | { tabler: 16 } | Tabler: 16px; other sets inherit 20px | | { default: 16 } | Tabler still inherits 28px; other sets: 16px | | 16 | All sets: 16px; replaces the inherited size map | File: IconConfigExample.astro ``` --- import { Icon, createIconConfig } from "@icones/astro" const config = { defaultSize: 24, } const scope = createIconConfig(config) const toolbarScope = createIconConfig({ defaultSize: 16, }, scope) --- ``` Note: Explicit icon properties win over scope defaults. Child maps merge by set and inherit the parent fallback; a child shared size, stroke width or boolean replaces that option’s whole map. sizeValues merges preset keys within each set; a flat dictionary updates shared presets without removing inherited set overrides. Appearance-only scopes share the parent’s store. - [Next: share colors with CSS](/guide/astro/global-styling) #### Local icon data Use sources to register artwork yourself, for example when icon names come from application state. The example maps an exact name to [tag, attributes] tuples and works without an HTTP service. Local sources are checked before the fallback API; child sources take priority over inherited sources. Set api to false to disable fallback API loading. This does not disable explicit per-icon loaders, lazy source functions or statically compiled icons. Use trusted artwork; icon data is not an HTML sanitizer. Choose the smallest registration that fits your use case. A full name registers one icon; a set prefix registers an Iconify collection. Do not pass a collection to data or altData: those properties accept one icon only. The second example shows the collection format without requiring another package. | Source form | When to use it | | --- | --- | | sources: { "app:check": data } | A few application icons, available immediately | | sources: { app: collection } | Several named icons from one Iconify collection | | sources: { "app:check": async () => data } | Load one icon lazily when its runtime name is requested | | data / altData | Inline a single icon without looking up a name | File: IconConfigExample.astro ``` --- import { Icon, createIconConfig, type IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" const iconName = "app:check" const config = { api: false, sources: { "app:check": [ [ "path", { fill: "none", stroke: "currentColor", strokeWidth: "2", strokeLinecap: "round", strokeLinejoin: "round", d: "m5 12 4 4L19 6", key: "0", }, ], ], }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions const scope = createIconConfig(config) --- ``` File: icon-sources.ts ``` import type { IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" export const config = { api: false, sources: { app: { prefix: "app", width: 24, height: 24, icons: { check: { body: '', }, }, }, }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` Note: The variable iconName leaves this application-owned name to runtime sources instead of Vite extraction. You can also import a tuple JSON file, such as icons/brand/data/4chan.json, and register it as sources: { "brand:4chan": parseElementData(logoJSON) }. Keep the imported array intact; do not wrap it in a body property. #### Load icons from an API Use api when a name is not available through static extraction or local sources. The fetch configuration requests /.json?icons= from an Iconify-compatible service. Replace the example URL with your own deployed service; configuring api does not create a server. For external SVG symbols, use api: { type: "symbol", baseUrl: "/icons" } with a same-origin symbol service. Symbol mode creates a reference without fetching JSON in JavaScript. A custom API loader can also be supplied as a function. To route sets independently, pass a per-set map to api, as in the second example. Tabler uses fetch, Flag uses same-origin symbols, and default: false disables fallback requests for other sets. Each entry also accepts a URL string or custom loader function. Local sources still take priority; explicit per-icon loaders are not disabled by api: false. API maps inherit parent entries and the parent or application fallback. An entry replaces that set’s entire API configuration, rather than merging URL or request options. A shared API value, including false, replaces the whole inherited map. API option keys such as type, baseUrl, url and fetch are reserved for shared API objects, not set prefixes. Core has no Iconify package dependency. Without an api override, unresolved set:name icons load from https://.icones.go-slim.dev/data/.json. Local sources and Vite output take priority. Set api: false to disable network fallback; Vite fallbackToApi controls build-time extraction only. If your service serves one JSON file per icon instead of the collection endpoint, provide api.url. The third example requests /icon-data/tabler%3Astar.json; return a single icon object or tuple array. For a custom response envelope, use transform to extract supported icon data. Keep server secrets out of browser configuration. File: IconConfigExample.astro ``` --- import { Icon, createIconConfig, type IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" const iconName = "tabler:star" const config = { api: { type: "fetch", baseUrl: "https://icons.example.com/icons" }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions const scope = createIconConfig(config) --- ``` File: icon-api.ts ``` import type { IconApiConfig, IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" export const api = { tabler: { type: "fetch", baseUrl: "https://icons.example.com/icons" }, flag: { type: "symbol", baseUrl: "/icons" }, default: false, } satisfies IconApiConfig export const config = { api } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` File: custom-icon-api.ts ``` import type { IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/astro" export const config = { api: { type: "fetch", url: (name) => new URL( `/icon-data/${encodeURIComponent(name)}.json`, "https://icons.example.com", ), }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` Note: Runtime api and the Vite plugin’s build-time loadIcon are separate. Statically collected names bypass runtime loading. Server-side fetches need an absolute URL, as shown here. #### Shared stores and SSR Create an IconStore when you need explicit cache limits, timeouts, concurrency or preloading, then pass it through store. Configure sources and api on that store, not alongside it. Keep the store’s identity stable within a mounted application so rerenders reuse its cache. Create a separate store for each SSR request, not a module-level server singleton. Preload required icons before rendering and safely serialize store.snapshot() through your framework. Hydrate with createIconStore({ initialData, ... }) and enough maxEntries to retain the page’s icons. preparePageIcons below returns both the request’s store and its serializable data. Render the page with that same store; creating a second store would discard the preload. Transfer initialData through your framework’s escaped data mechanism, then call createAppIconStore(initialData) once for the browser application before hydration. Astro waits for icon loading on the server. Create request-local scopes in frontmatter; no client hydration is required for the SVG itself. - For a client-only application, create the store at its bootstrap boundary. In React, a lazy useState initializer also keeps one store per mounted root. Do not call createIconStore in every render or share a mutable server store between requests. - preload resolves after attempting every requested name; it is not a guarantee that every icon exists. Inspect getState(name).status when an icon is required. snapshot includes loaded data, not failed requests or external symbol references. - Concurrent requests for the same name share work within one store. maxEntries limits cached entries, concurrency limits active loads, and timeout is in milliseconds. Use store.retry(name) after a failure; getState alone never starts a request. File: icon-store.ts ``` import { createIconStore, type Data } from "@icones/astro" // Call once per client application, or once per SSR request. export const createAppIconStore = ( initialData?: Readonly>, ) => createIconStore({ api: { type: "fetch", baseUrl: "https://icons.example.com/icons" }, initialData, maxEntries: 512, concurrency: 4, timeout: 10_000, }) // Run in your server request handler before rendering the page. export async function preparePageIcons(names: readonly string[]) { const store = createAppIconStore() await store.preload(names) return { store, initialData: store.snapshot() } } // Pass the returned store to createIconConfig({ store }). // Do not pass sources or api alongside store; configure those on the store itself. ``` Note: For example, await preparePageIcons(["tabler:star", "tabler:heart"]) in the request handler. Do not interpolate JSON.stringify(initialData) directly into an HTML script: use your framework’s safe serialization. Astro can render the loaded SVG without creating a browser store; Vanilla initialization enhances HTML in the browser, not on the server. #### Troubleshooting configuration Check appearance and data loading separately. A valid size configuration cannot make missing artwork appear, and changing an API does not change artwork already embedded by Vite. For runtime names, inspect the store you actually passed to the icons. | Symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | Changing defaultSize has no effect | Remove the icon’s explicit size, then check the nearest child scope and the matching set entry. default does not override an inherited matching set. | | Per-set settings do not affect inline data | Anonymous data uses default. Register the data under a full name in sources and render that name when set-specific defaults are needed. | | Changing strokeWidth has no effect | Confirm the artwork uses SVG strokes rather than filled paths. absoluteStrokeWidth needs a numeric pixel size to keep its rendered thickness fixed. | | An icon is blank | Check the exact set:name, registered sources and network response. missing means no data was found; error indicates a loader failure. A referenced symbol still depends on the browser loading a valid same-origin SVG URL. | | Changing sources or api has no effect | If you supplied store, configure loading on that store. If Vite embedded the name, change the build-time data or use a runtime name for this example. | | Requests repeat or SSR icons disappear | Keep the store stable, preload into the store used to render, and restore its initialData before hydration. Do not recreate the store inside every render. | #### Option reference The component providers and explicit scopes share these options. Use defaultSize, not size, on configuration; color, fill, rotate and accessibility labels belong on individual icons or in CSS. defaultSize accepts one size for every icon, or a map such as { tabler: "lg", default: "md" }. Keys are set prefixes, not categories or styles. An individual size takes priority, followed by the matching set, then default, then the built-in md (20px). Map values can also be numbers or CSS lengths. The same set/default format also applies to sizeValues, strokeWidth, absoluteStrokeWidth and api. Individual icon properties take priority over appearance defaults. The currently displayed alternative determines the set. Anonymous tuple/JSON data uses default. Register collections in sources and select an icon by name to apply its set defaults. sources and store keep their existing formats. | Option | Default / behavior | | --- | --- | | defaultSize | md (20px); accepts a size or a set-to-size map with a default fallback | | sizeValues | xs: 12, sm: 16, md: 20, lg: 24, xl: 28; shared or per-set preset dictionaries, merged by preset key | | strokeWidth | 1.5 on a 24-unit canvas; a number or a set-to-number map with default | | absoluteStrokeWidth | false; a boolean or a set-to-boolean map with default; enable with numeric pixel dimensions for a fixed rendered stroke | | sources | Local data, sets or lazy loaders; inherits parent sources | | api | Shared or per-set API with default; inherits the parent or application fallback; false disables requests for the selected set | | store | An existing IconStore; takes priority over sources and api on the same configuration |

chapters.title: TypeScript
chapters.markdown:
### TypeScript

[Source](/guide/astro/typescript)

Keep icon props and local JSON data checked at the boundary.

#### Check your props

Each adapter exports IconProps. Use satisfies to check an object while retaining the specific values inferred by TypeScript.

IconName is provided by the lightweight @icones/names package and re-exported by every adapter, without installing the icon artwork. Use satisfies IconName to validate an exact bundled name, including its style suffix. IconName<"tabler"> narrows suggestions to one set. Name and IconProps still accept dynamic strings and custom sources; they do not guarantee that a name exists in the local collection.

File: icon-props.ts

```
import type { IconName, IconProps } from "@icones/astro"

const iconProps = {
  name: "tabler:star" satisfies IconName,
  size: 24,
  color: "#7712f7",
} satisfies IconProps
```

#### Validate local JSON

JSON copied from the Icons page contains SVG node tuples. TypeScript infers JSON imports as ordinary arrays; parseElementData validates them and returns typed ElementData. Pass the result to the icon’s data prop.

File: star-data.ts

```
import { parseElementData } from "@icones/astro"
import starJSON from "./icons/tabler/data/star.json"

const star = parseElementData(starJSON)
```

#### Know your data format

Use the format that matches your source: JSON from the Icons page contains [tag, attributes] tuples; an Iconify icon object contains width, height and body. Both are supported. Do not put a tuple array inside a body property or pass SVG markup to parseElementData.

chapters.title: Accessibility
chapters.markdown:
### Accessibility

[Source](/guide/astro/accessibility)

Decide whether the icon adds meaning or simply accompanies visible text.

#### Decorative icons

Unlabelled icons are hidden from assistive technology by default. This is appropriate when adjacent text already explains the action, such as an icon next to the word Search.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:search"
  size={20}
/>
```

#### Meaningful icons

Give an icon that conveys information its own accessible label. role="img" identifies it as an image; aria-label provides the text alternative.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:check"
  size={20}
  role="img"
  aria-label="Completed"
/>
```

#### Interactive controls

For an icon-only action, use a real button or link and label that control. Keep the icon decorative inside it. The SVG should not have to reproduce keyboard focus, activation and disabled behavior itself.

Do not rely on color alone to communicate a state, and keep labels meaningful when switching to alternative artwork.

chapters.title: Alternative
chapters.markdown:
### Alternative

[Source](/guide/astro/alternative)

Switch between primary and alternative artwork, using names or inline data.

#### Define an alternative

altName identifies the second icon. showAlt selects it; false or an omitted attribute keeps the primary name.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"
---

<Icon
  name="tabler:star"
  altName="tabler:star-filled"
  showAlt={true}
  size={24}
/>
```

#### Use inline data for either state

data and altData accept an individual Iconify data object or an element tuple array. You can use names for both states, data for both states, or a name in one group and data in the other.

Do not pass a name string or an entire icon collection to data or altData. Register collections in sources, then select the primary and alternative icons with name and altName.

Choose one source per group: name or data for the primary icon, altName or altData for the alternative. Providing both in either group logs console.error; data or altData still takes priority, even if that group is not currently shown.

With showAlt enabled, altData takes priority over altName. Without an alternative source, the primary icon remains selected. A missing or failed alternative does not switch back to the primary icon.

File: IconExample.astro

```
---
import { Icon } from "@icones/astro"

const primary = { body: '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8"/>' }
const alternative = { body: '<path d="M5 12l4 4 10-10" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>' }
---

<Icon data={primary} altData={alternative} showAlt={true} />
```

Note: For a whole icon set, register it in sources and select icons by name or altName instead of passing the set alongside a name prop.

#### Follow application state

Set showAlt from your server-side state when rendering the page. For changes after page load, use a client framework component or the vanilla adapter.

#### An alternative is not a fallback

Alternative selection is intentional, not an error recovery mechanism. If the active drawing cannot load, use fallback content or handle the loading state. The adapter does not invent a filled counterpart.

chapters.title: Global Styling
Standard elements overview
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Standard elements overview [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/overview) Use ordinary i elements with icon-* attributes. This tutorial follows the standard-element entry from your first icon through configuration. #### 1. Start with this HTML Write an i element with icon-name and import @icones/vanilla/standard-element once. The initializer finds those hosts and appends an SVG without replacing the original i. Both the import and artwork are required. Complete Getting started to connect Vite and your local JSON before running this example. The SVG lives in light DOM, without Shadow DOM. File: index.html ``` ``` - [Follow this path: install and display your first icon](/guide/vanilla/standard/getting-started) #### 2. Change attributes Add only the attributes you need. Empty or true enables a boolean option; false disables it. Removing an attribute restores the configured default. Only i[icon-name] opts into rendering. Other tags, a bare icon attribute, and data-icon* aliases are not scanned. Native class, style and aria-* remain on the i; icon-class, icon-label and icon-role target its SVG. | HTML attribute | Purpose | | --- | --- | | icon-name | Exact icon name, e.g. tabler:star | | icon-size | A named size preset, pixel value or CSS length | | icon-color | CSS color used by currentColor in the SVG | | icon-stroke-width | Outline weight; original preserves the source | | icon-rotate | Quarter turns: 1 = 90° | | icon-alt-name | The exact name of an alternative icon; no suffix is inferred | | icon-show-alt | true selects altName; false keeps the primary icon | | icon-label | Accessible label on the SVG | File: index.html ``` ``` - [Compare prop support and Vite modes](/guide/rendering) #### 3. Let the element update Change an attribute with setAttribute("icon-size", "32"). A MutationObserver synchronizes the SVG; adding or removing matching i elements starts or stops rendering automatically. For a custom root or shared defaults, replace the automatic import with bindIcons({ root, scope }). Its handle provides refresh(), load() and destroy(). Repeated initialization of one root and attrPrefix returns the existing handle; it does not replace its scope. - [Configure this element’s defaults](/guide/vanilla/standard/icon-config) #### 4. Defer the first render Add icon-defer="intersect" to render when the host enters the viewport, or icon-defer="domready" to wait for DOMContentLoaded. If the document is already interactive or complete, domready renders immediately. No SVG or runtime data request starts before activation. After the first render, updates proceed normally. Removing a pending host cancels its wait; load() does not force activation. File: index.html ``` ``` Note: Without IntersectionObserver, intersect renders immediately. Reserve space with CSS if needed. Static Vite data is still bundled; deferred rendering is not code splitting. #### 5. Customize the attribute prefix If icon-* does not fit your app, replace the automatic standard-element import with explicit initialization. attrPrefix includes the trailing hyphen and changes every icon attribute, not just its name. Keep the same prefix in Vite’s attrPrefixes list so build-time collection can find your HTML names. That list replaces the default; use [icon-, ui-] only if you intentionally use both. Initializers are keyed by root and attrPrefix. Use one active name prefix per host. File: index.html ``` ``` File: vite.config.ts ``` import { defineConfig } from "vite" import { icones } from "@icones/vite" export default defineConfig({ plugins: [icones({ dataDir: "./icons", attrPrefixes: ["ui-"], })], }) ``` Note: Prefixes start with a lowercase letter, use lowercase letters/digits and hyphens, and end with a hyphen. There is no implicit fallback to icon-* or data-*.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Getting started [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/getting-started) Display one Standard elements icon, check that it works, then change its appearance. No shared configuration is needed yet. Before you start: Start with an existing Vanilla application using Vite. Run the commands from its root directory; this tutorial does not scaffold a new app. Outcome: A visible star icon that you can resize and recolor with a single prop. #### 1. Install the packages The adapter renders SVGs. The Vite plugin finds literal icon names in your code and includes their artwork in your build. Run these commands inside your application. File: Terminal ``` bun add @icones/vanilla bun add -d @icones/vite ``` Run these commands in your application directory. They require access to the @icones packages in your registry; if a package is unavailable, obtain a compatible release before continuing. Check your result: Your app has both @icones/vanilla and @icones/vite in its dependencies. #### 2. Connect the artwork Add icones to your existing plugin list; keep your framework’s other plugins. Set dataDir to the directory containing your icon JSON files. This example assumes icons is inside the application root. On the Icons page, find tabler:star, open its JSON tab and save the original JSON as icons/tabler/data/star.json in your application. Keep the collection’s license from the Licenses page with any artwork you use. Update vite.config.ts, then restart your Vite development server so it reads the new plugin configuration. File: vite.config.ts ``` import { defineConfig } from "vite" import { icones } from "@icones/vite" export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ // Keep your existing framework plugin here. icones({ mode: "symbol", dataDir: "./icons", emitData: false, }), ], }) ``` File: project-layout.txt ``` your-app/ icons/tabler/data/star.json vite.config.ts ``` Note: Use the original tuple JSON from the JSON tab, not SVG markup. Save other icons with the same /data/.json layout. Set fallbackToApi: false to prevent build-time requests for missing icons. Check your result: The file icons/tabler/data/star.json exists in your application. dataDir points to ./icons, the folder containing tabler/, not to the JSON file itself. - [Vite and API loading](/guide/loading) #### 3. Display your first icon Add this to index.html. Write an ordinary i with icon-name and import @icones/vanilla/standard-element once. The initializer scans matching hosts and appends an SVG directly inside each i. Keep the icon in HTML. Run your app with its normal development command and open the page. Verify the star is visible before continuing. File: icon.html ``` ``` Check your result: You see one 24px star. In the DOM it contains an SVG; no IconConfig or runtime API setup is required. #### 4. Change one thing at a time In the previous example, change icon-size from 24 to 32. Once the star grows, add icon-color to make it purple. Keep the name and loading setup unchanged. This complete replacement example combines those two changes. Remove icon-color to follow the surrounding text color again. File: icon.html ``` ``` Check your result: The same star is now 32px and purple. You changed its presentation, not its source JSON. - [Next: color, sizing and stroke](/guide/vanilla/standard/color) - [Then: Standard elements attributes and deferred rendering](/guide/vanilla/standard/overview) - [Later: share defaults with IconConfig](/guide/vanilla/standard/icon-config) #### If the icon does not appear Check these in order before adding configuration. Shared defaults cannot fix a missing import, an incorrect path or missing artwork. Reference section (optional). - Check the terminal for a missing-package or missing-icon error. - Confirm the icon’s name is exactly tabler:star, and dataDir contains tabler/data/star.json. - Restart the development server after changing its configuration. - Use a Vite-served page, not a file:// URL. Confirm the module script imports @icones/vanilla/standard-element and the host uses i with icon-name. - Check that CSS is not hiding the SVG or giving it the same color as the background. - Use a literal name for this lesson. Computed names need local data or a runtime loading setup; learn that after the first icon works.

chapters.title: Color
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Color [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/color) Let icons follow your text, or give a single icon its own color. #### Inherit text color Monochrome icons use currentColor. When icon-color is omitted, the drawing follows the surrounding text color, so it fits naturally inside links, buttons and status messages. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Set an explicit color The icon-color option accepts a CSS color. Use a hex value, a named color, or a design token such as var(--accent-color). File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Color in Outline, Filled and Solid icons The SVG color value does not replace every fill or stroke. It affects only paint values that use currentColor. The artwork decides whether that color appears on an outline or a filled area. Outline, Filled and Solid describe the artwork, not color modes. Select the exact icon name to change styles; setting color or fill does not turn an outline drawing into its designed filled counterpart. | Style | What changes with color | | --- | --- | | Outline | Usually colors strokes (stroke="currentColor") while fill="none" keeps the center empty. Example: tabler:star. | | Filled | Usually colors the solid shape through fill="currentColor". Example: tabler:star-filled. It does not add a separate outline. | | Solid | The same color behavior as Filled, with the collection’s own naming. Example: bootstrap:star-fill. | Note: Judge by the SVG paint values, not just the style label. For example, bootstrap:star draws a hollow outline with a filled path, while the bundled phosphor:star uses a currentColor stroke. - [Collection differences](/guide/collections) #### Respect multicolor artwork A drawing with fixed fill or stroke colors keeps those colors. currentColor only affects paths designed to inherit it; it does not recolor every path in a flag or brand mark.

chapters.title: Sizing
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Sizing [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/sizing) Use a shared size preset, a pixel value, or a CSS length. #### Named presets The built-in presets cover common interface sizes. Your application can override its defaults. | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 12px | 16px | 20px | 24px | 28px | File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Pixels and CSS lengths A numeric icon-size is measured in pixels. A CSS length, such as 1.5rem or 1em, lets the icon follow your type scale. It controls both dimensions. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Canvas versus display size The original viewBox describes the drawing’s coordinates, not its rendered pixel size. A 24 × 24 drawing can be displayed at 64px without rewriting the source data. To set separate icon-width and icon-height values, omit icon-size. An explicit size takes priority over both.

chapters.title: Stroke Width
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Stroke Width [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/stroke-width) Adjust icons drawn with SVG strokes. Filled paths keep their original shape. #### Set the outline weight icon-stroke-width uses a normalized 24-unit basis. This makes the same value usable across collections with different source canvas dimensions. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Keep a constant pixel weight Set icon-absolute-stroke-width with a numeric pixel size to keep the stroke’s rendered thickness steady as the icon gets larger. This calculation uses the resolved width and height, not a browser layout measurement. Numeric pixels and px strings work; relative CSS units or a later CSS size override do not guarantee a fixed pixel stroke. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Preserve the original drawing Use icon-stroke-width="original" to preserve the source width. Filled artwork does not gain an outline just because a stroke width is set. Multicolor artwork with fixed stroke colors is excluded from automatic path stroke rewriting. An Outline label does not guarantee editable strokes: bootstrap:star is a filled path. Phosphor Regular uses strokes that respond to strokeWidth, while Phosphor Fill uses filled shapes that keep their geometry. Omitting strokeWidth still uses the shared default of 1.5, in both svg and symbol modes. Component props accept a numeric width; there is no cross-framework strokeWidth="original" value. Set an explicit weight when you need a thinner or bolder drawing. - [Prop support](/guide/prop-support)

chapters.title: Fill
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Fill [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/fill) Choose artwork intentionally: outline and filled icons are independent drawings. #### Choose the filled drawing Use the exact filled icon name from the collection. For example, tabler:star and tabler:star-filled are two different icons. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Understand SVG fill The fill attribute is inherited by paths that do not set their own fill. It does not replace a path’s explicit fill="none", and it cannot turn an outline into a carefully designed filled variant. For custom tuple data, specify fill in the artwork. Inline rendering can supply a missing fill from the prop, but generated symbols bake missing root fills as none; the root SVG fill prop cannot override that explicit value. Note: Do not guess a -filled name. Some collections use different names, or do not include a corresponding filled drawing. - [Collection differences](/guide/collections) #### Switch between variants Use icon-alt-name and icon-show-alt when an icon has two known states. The Alternative guide explains explicit variant selection. File: icon.html ``` ```

chapters.title: IconConfig
chapters.markdown:
### Standard elements · IconConfig [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/icon-config) Configure ordinary i elements with createIconConfig and bindIcons. Customize appearance first, then choose local sources, an API or a shared store. #### Basic usage Configuration is optional. Without custom settings, icons use the built-in md size (20px) and a stroke width of 1.5. Add shared configuration when several icons should use the same defaults. Consider an article toolbar: its main actions need 24px icons, while a compact action needs a 16px icon. Set the common value once, then override only the exception. The example demonstrates icon configuration; connect the buttons to your own application actions. In index.html, replace the @icones/vanilla/standard-element import with the script below, then reload. createIconConfig creates a scope: an object holding shared settings. bindIcons({ scope }) uses it for the i elements it observes. Keep the icons in HTML. Keep your existing loading setup. With Vite, include tabler/data/star.json and tabler/data/heart.json in dataDir for these examples. Shared appearance settings do not load artwork. - Reuse the same scope for icons that should share defaults. Creating a scope does not change unrelated icons elsewhere on the page. - defaultSize belongs to shared configuration; size belongs to one icon. Removing the explicit size makes that icon inherit the shared value again. - Button text supplies the accessible name; the icons remain decorative. Configuration affects Icones icons, not arbitrary SVG elements or the button’s CSS layout. File: index.html ```
``` Note: Remove the automatic standard-element import; do not keep it beside explicit initialization. Repeating bindIcons for the same root and attrPrefix returns its first handle without replacing its scope. Reload the page to try the replacement example. Check your result: The first two buttons contain 24 × 24 icons, and the compact action contains a 16 × 16 icon. Change defaultSize to 20: only the first two change; the explicit 16px override stays the same. - [First, display an icon](/guide/vanilla/standard/getting-started) #### Customize appearance Use sizeValues to customize named size presets, defaultSize to choose a shared size or a size for each set, and strokeWidth to set the outline weight. Omitted settings keep their inherited defaults. In this example, Tabler uses lg at 28px and a fixed 2px stroke; other sets use md at 20px and a normalized stroke width of 1.5. The heart uses an explicit size of 32, overriding its set’s default size. defaultSize, sizeValues, strokeWidth and absoluteStrokeWidth accept shared values or maps keyed by set. Use default for unmatched sets. For sizeValues, each set contains its own preset dictionary; missing presets fall back to default, then the built-in values. The original flat form, such as sizeValues: { lg: 28 }, still works for shared presets. - Use named sizes such as sm and lg as design tokens. Change sizeValues once to update all icons using that preset; a numeric size such as 32 does not use the preset dictionary. - A normalized strokeWidth of 1.5 renders at 1.5px on a 24px icon and scales with its size. absoluteStrokeWidth keeps the rendered stroke fixed when the icon has a numeric pixel size; it does not change filled artwork. - Keep color on the icon or inherit it from CSS currentColor. IconConfig has no shared color or fill option. A per-icon strokeWidth or absoluteStrokeWidth overrides the corresponding scope setting. | Icon in this example | Resolved size | Rendered stroke | | --- | --- | --- | | tabler:star | 28px — Tabler’s lg preset | 2px — fixed | | lucide:star | 20px — default md preset | 1.25px — 1.5 × 20 / 24 | | tabler:heart | 32px — explicit size | 2px — fixed | File: index.html ``` ``` Note: The Tabler star is 28px, the Lucide star is 20px and the heart is 32px. With Vite, also add lucide/data/star.json to dataDir. strokeWidth affects SVG strokes, not outlines drawn with filled paths. #### Configuration inheritance Use a child configuration when one part of the interface needs different defaults. Here the page uses 24px icons and the toolbar uses 16px. These examples are independent of the custom presets above. Create a child scope by passing the original scope as the second argument. Initialize two separate roots: page-icons uses the page scope and toolbar uses toolbarScope. Replace the previous example and reload; do not keep a document-wide initializer that would already own both groups. | Child defaultSize | With parent { tabler: 28, default: 20 } | | --- | --- | | Not set | Tabler: 28px; other sets: 20px | | { tabler: 16 } | Tabler: 16px; other sets inherit 20px | | { default: 16 } | Tabler still inherits 28px; other sets: 16px | | 16 | All sets: 16px; replaces the inherited size map | File: index.html ```
``` Note: Explicit icon properties win over scope defaults. Child maps merge by set and inherit the parent fallback; a child shared size, stroke width or boolean replaces that option’s whole map. sizeValues merges preset keys within each set; a flat dictionary updates shared presets without removing inherited set overrides. Appearance-only scopes share the parent’s store. - [Next: share colors with CSS](/guide/vanilla/standard/global-styling) #### Local icon data Use sources to register artwork yourself, for example when icon names come from application state. The example maps an exact name to [tag, attributes] tuples and works without an HTTP service. Local sources are checked before the fallback API; child sources take priority over inherited sources. Set api to false to disable fallback API loading. This does not disable explicit per-icon loaders, lazy source functions or statically compiled icons. Use trusted artwork; icon data is not an HTML sanitizer. Choose the smallest registration that fits your use case. A full name registers one icon; a set prefix registers an Iconify collection. Do not pass a collection to data or altData: those properties accept one icon only. The second example shows the collection format without requiring another package. | Source form | When to use it | | --- | --- | | sources: { "app:check": data } | A few application icons, available immediately | | sources: { app: collection } | Several named icons from one Iconify collection | | sources: { "app:check": async () => data } | Load one icon lazily when its runtime name is requested | | data / altData | Inline a single icon without looking up a name | File: index.html ``` ``` File: icon-sources.ts ``` import type { IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/vanilla" export const config = { api: false, sources: { app: { prefix: "app", width: 24, height: 24, icons: { check: { body: '', }, }, }, }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` Note: The variable iconName leaves this application-owned name to runtime sources instead of Vite extraction. You can also import a tuple JSON file, such as icons/brand/data/4chan.json, and register it as sources: { "brand:4chan": parseElementData(logoJSON) }. Keep the imported array intact; do not wrap it in a body property. #### Load icons from an API Use api when a name is not available through static extraction or local sources. The fetch configuration requests /.json?icons= from an Iconify-compatible service. Replace the example URL with your own deployed service; configuring api does not create a server. For external SVG symbols, use api: { type: "symbol", baseUrl: "/icons" } with a same-origin symbol service. Symbol mode creates a reference without fetching JSON in JavaScript. A custom API loader can also be supplied as a function. To route sets independently, pass a per-set map to api, as in the second example. Tabler uses fetch, Flag uses same-origin symbols, and default: false disables fallback requests for other sets. Each entry also accepts a URL string or custom loader function. Local sources still take priority; explicit per-icon loaders are not disabled by api: false. API maps inherit parent entries and the parent or application fallback. An entry replaces that set’s entire API configuration, rather than merging URL or request options. A shared API value, including false, replaces the whole inherited map. API option keys such as type, baseUrl, url and fetch are reserved for shared API objects, not set prefixes. Core has no Iconify package dependency. Without an api override, unresolved set:name icons load from https://.icones.go-slim.dev/data/.json. Local sources and Vite output take priority. Set api: false to disable network fallback; Vite fallbackToApi controls build-time extraction only. If your service serves one JSON file per icon instead of the collection endpoint, provide api.url. The third example requests /icon-data/tabler%3Astar.json; return a single icon object or tuple array. For a custom response envelope, use transform to extract supported icon data. Keep server secrets out of browser configuration. File: index.html ``` ``` File: icon-api.ts ``` import type { IconApiConfig, IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/vanilla" export const api = { tabler: { type: "fetch", baseUrl: "https://icons.example.com/icons" }, flag: { type: "symbol", baseUrl: "/icons" }, default: false, } satisfies IconApiConfig export const config = { api } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` File: custom-icon-api.ts ``` import type { IconScopeOptions } from "@icones/vanilla" export const config = { api: { type: "fetch", url: (name) => new URL( `/icon-data/${encodeURIComponent(name)}.json`, "https://icons.example.com", ), }, } satisfies IconScopeOptions // Pass config to createIconConfig, then assign the scope as in Basic usage. ``` Note: Runtime api and the Vite plugin’s build-time loadIcon are separate. Statically collected names bypass runtime loading. Server-side fetches need an absolute URL, as shown here. #### Shared stores and SSR Create an IconStore when you need explicit cache limits, timeouts, concurrency or preloading, then pass it through store. Configure sources and api on that store, not alongside it. Keep the store’s identity stable within a mounted application so rerenders reuse its cache. Create a separate store for each SSR request, not a module-level server singleton. Preload required icons before rendering and safely serialize store.snapshot() through your framework. Hydrate with createIconStore({ initialData, ... }) and enough maxEntries to retain the page’s icons. preparePageIcons below returns both the request’s store and its serializable data. Render the page with that same store; creating a second store would discard the preload. Transfer initialData through your framework’s escaped data mechanism, then call createAppIconStore(initialData) once for the browser application before hydration. The standard initializer is safe to import on the server and is a no-op without a DOM. In a browser it observes its configured root. Keep each handle and call destroy() when that view is disposed; removing individual hosts releases their SVG subscriptions. Use core renderIcon for server-generated SVG. - For a client-only application, create the store at its bootstrap boundary. In React, a lazy useState initializer also keeps one store per mounted root. Do not call createIconStore in every render or share a mutable server store between requests. - preload resolves after attempting every requested name; it is not a guarantee that every icon exists. Inspect getState(name).status when an icon is required. snapshot includes loaded data, not failed requests or external symbol references. - Concurrent requests for the same name share work within one store. maxEntries limits cached entries, concurrency limits active loads, and timeout is in milliseconds. Use store.retry(name) after a failure; getState alone never starts a request. File: icon-store.ts ``` import { createIconStore, type Data } from "@icones/vanilla" // Call once per client application, or once per SSR request. export const createAppIconStore = ( initialData?: Readonly>, ) => createIconStore({ api: { type: "fetch", baseUrl: "https://icons.example.com/icons" }, initialData, maxEntries: 512, concurrency: 4, timeout: 10_000, }) // Run in your server request handler before rendering the page. export async function preparePageIcons(names: readonly string[]) { const store = createAppIconStore() await store.preload(names) return { store, initialData: store.snapshot() } } // Pass the returned store to createIconConfig({ store }). // Do not pass sources or api alongside store; configure those on the store itself. ``` Note: For example, await preparePageIcons(["tabler:star", "tabler:heart"]) in the request handler. Do not interpolate JSON.stringify(initialData) directly into an HTML script: use your framework’s safe serialization. Astro can render the loaded SVG without creating a browser store; Vanilla initialization enhances HTML in the browser, not on the server. #### Troubleshooting configuration Check appearance and data loading separately. A valid size configuration cannot make missing artwork appear, and changing an API does not change artwork already embedded by Vite. For runtime names, inspect the store you actually passed to the icons. | Symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | Changing defaultSize has no effect | Remove the icon’s explicit size, then check the nearest child scope and the matching set entry. default does not override an inherited matching set. | | Per-set settings do not affect inline data | Anonymous data uses default. Register the data under a full name in sources and render that name when set-specific defaults are needed. | | Changing strokeWidth has no effect | Confirm the artwork uses SVG strokes rather than filled paths. absoluteStrokeWidth needs a numeric pixel size to keep its rendered thickness fixed. | | An icon is blank | Check the exact set:name, registered sources and network response. missing means no data was found; error indicates a loader failure. A referenced symbol still depends on the browser loading a valid same-origin SVG URL. | | Changing sources or api has no effect | If you supplied store, configure loading on that store. If Vite embedded the name, change the build-time data or use a runtime name for this example. | | Requests repeat or SSR icons disappear | Keep the store stable, preload into the store used to render, and restore its initialData before hydration. Do not recreate the store inside every render. | #### Option reference The component providers and explicit scopes share these options. Use defaultSize, not size, on configuration; color, fill, rotate and accessibility labels belong on individual icons or in CSS. defaultSize accepts one size for every icon, or a map such as { tabler: "lg", default: "md" }. Keys are set prefixes, not categories or styles. An individual size takes priority, followed by the matching set, then default, then the built-in md (20px). Map values can also be numbers or CSS lengths. The same set/default format also applies to sizeValues, strokeWidth, absoluteStrokeWidth and api. Individual icon properties take priority over appearance defaults. The currently displayed alternative determines the set. Anonymous tuple/JSON data uses default. Register collections in sources and select an icon by name to apply its set defaults. sources and store keep their existing formats. | Option | Default / behavior | | --- | --- | | defaultSize | md (20px); accepts a size or a set-to-size map with a default fallback | | sizeValues | xs: 12, sm: 16, md: 20, lg: 24, xl: 28; shared or per-set preset dictionaries, merged by preset key | | strokeWidth | 1.5 on a 24-unit canvas; a number or a set-to-number map with default | | absoluteStrokeWidth | false; a boolean or a set-to-boolean map with default; enable with numeric pixel dimensions for a fixed rendered stroke | | sources | Local data, sets or lazy loaders; inherits parent sources | | api | Shared or per-set API with default; inherits the parent or application fallback; false disables requests for the selected set | | store | An existing IconStore; takes priority over sources and api on the same configuration |

chapters.title: TypeScript
chapters.markdown:
### Standard elements · TypeScript

[Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/typescript)

Type-check the initialization and updates for your selected HTML element.

#### Type the initialization options

Use IconBindingOptions for the initializer, not IconProps on the HTML host. HTML icon-* attributes remain strings.

File: main.ts

```
import { bindIcons, type IconBindingOptions } from "@icones/vanilla"

const options = {
  root: document,
  attrPrefix: "icon-",
} satisfies IconBindingOptions

const icons = bindIcons(options)
```

#### Update the HTML attribute

IconName is provided by the lightweight @icones/names package and re-exported by the adapter. Validate a name with satisfies IconName before assigning it to an HTML attribute; native setAttribute and literal HTML attributes are still strings, not compile-time name checks.

Keep native DOM types on i. The initializer’s handle waits for mounted icons; it does not force deferred hosts to activate.

File: main.ts

```
import { bindIcons, type IconName } from "@icones/vanilla"

const name = "tabler:star" satisfies IconName
const icons = bindIcons()
const icon = document.querySelector("i[icon-name]")
icon?.setAttribute("icon-name", name)
icon?.setAttribute("icon-size", "32")
await icons?.load()
```

#### Validate local JSON

Use parseElementData to validate imported tuple JSON before adding it to a scope’s sources. HTML hosts do not have a JSON data attribute. The configuration chapter shows how to connect sources to this element.

File: star-data.ts

```
import { parseElementData } from "@icones/vanilla"
import starJSON from "./icons/tabler/data/star.json"

export const star = parseElementData(starJSON)
```

- [Register local data for this element](/guide/vanilla/standard/icon-config)

chapters.title: Accessibility
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Accessibility [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/accessibility) Decide whether the icon adds meaning or simply accompanies visible text. #### Decorative icons Unlabelled icons are hidden from assistive technology by default. This is appropriate when adjacent text already explains the action, such as an icon next to the word Search. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Meaningful icons Use icon-role="img" and icon-label to label the generated SVG. Native role and aria-label remain on the host. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Interactive controls For an icon-only action, use a real button or link and label that control. Keep the icon decorative inside it. The SVG should not have to reproduce keyboard focus, activation and disabled behavior itself. Do not rely on color alone to communicate a state, and keep labels meaningful when switching to alternative artwork.

chapters.title: Alternative
chapters.markdown: ### Standard elements · Alternative [Source](/guide/vanilla/standard/alternative) Switch between primary and alternative artwork, using names or inline data. #### Define an alternative icon-alt-name identifies the second icon. icon-show-alt selects it; false or an omitted attribute keeps the primary name. File: icon.html ``` ``` #### Use inline data for either state data and altData accept an individual Iconify data object or an element tuple array. You can use names for both states, data for both states, or a name in one group and data in the other. Do not pass a name string or an entire icon collection to data or altData. Register collections in sources, then select the primary and alternative icons with name and altName. Choose one source per group: name or data for the primary icon, altName or altData for the alternative. Providing both in either group logs console.error; data or altData still takes priority, even if that group is not currently shown. With showAlt enabled, altData takes priority over altName. Without an alternative source, the primary icon remains selected. A missing or failed alternative does not switch back to the primary icon. File: main.ts ``` import { createIcon } from "@icones/vanilla" const primary = { body: '' } const alternative = { body: '' } const icon = createIcon({ data: primary, altData: alternative }) document.body.append(icon.element) icon.update({ data: primary, altData: alternative, showAlt: true }) // Call icon.destroy() when the owner is removed. ``` Note: Object-valued data and altData belong to the JavaScript createIcon/mountIcon API, not HTML attributes. For standard elements and Web Components, register data in sources and use the name and alternative-name attributes. #### Follow application state Keep icon-name and icon-alt-name on the host, then use element.setAttribute("icon-show-alt", "true") or "false". The standard initializer observes the change. #### An alternative is not a fallback Alternative selection is intentional, not an error recovery mechanism. If the active drawing cannot load, use fallback content or handle the loading state. The adapter does not invent a filled counterpart.

chapters.title: Global Styling
Web Components overview
chapters.markdown:
### Web Components · Web Components overview

[Source](/guide/vanilla/web/overview)

Use the dedicated icones-icon tag. This tutorial follows the web-element entry from your first icon through configuration.

#### 1. Start with this HTML

Write an icones-icon element with name and import @icones/vanilla/web-element once. The browser upgrades the tag and appends an SVG when it is connected.

Both the import and artwork are required. Complete Getting started to connect Vite and your local JSON before running this example. The SVG lives in light DOM, without Shadow DOM.

File: index.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="24"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

- [Follow this path: install and display your first icon](/guide/vanilla/web/getting-started)

#### 2. Change attributes

Add only the attributes you need. Empty or true enables a boolean option; false disables it. Removing an attribute restores the configured default.

Only the dedicated tag opts into rendering. Native class, style and aria-* remain on the host; svg-class, label and svg-role target its SVG. Use decorative, not the native hidden attribute, for decorative icons.

| HTML attribute | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| name | Exact icon name, e.g. tabler:star |
| size | A named size preset, pixel value or CSS length |
| color | CSS color used by currentColor in the SVG |
| stroke-width | Outline weight; original preserves the source |
| rotate | Quarter turns: 1 = 90° |
| alt-name | The exact name of an alternative icon; no suffix is inferred |
| show-alt | true selects altName; false keeps the primary icon |
| label | Accessible label on the SVG |

File: index.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="32"
  color="#7712f7"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

- [Compare prop support and Vite modes](/guide/rendering)

#### 3. Let the element update

Change an attribute with setAttribute("size", "32"). The Web Component lifecycle synchronizes the SVG immediately; connecting or removing a tag starts or stops rendering automatically.

For shared defaults, replace the automatic import with defineIconElement({ scope }). Register once per window; repeated registration does not change its defaults. A specific icon can use its own scope object through element.scope.

- [Configure this element’s defaults](/guide/vanilla/web/icon-config)

#### 4. Defer the first render

Add defer="intersect" to render when the host enters the viewport, or defer="domready" to wait for DOMContentLoaded. If the document is already interactive or complete, domready renders immediately.

No SVG or runtime data request starts before activation. After the first render, updates proceed normally. Removing a pending host cancels its wait; load() does not force activation.

File: index.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="24"
  defer="intersect"
></icones-icon>

<icones-icon
  name="tabler:heart"
  size="24"
  defer="domready"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

Note: Without IntersectionObserver, intersect renders immediately. Reserve space with CSS if needed. Static Vite data is still bundled; deferred rendering is not code splitting.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.markdown:
### Web Components · Getting started

[Source](/guide/vanilla/web/getting-started)

Display one Web Components icon, check that it works, then change its appearance. No shared configuration is needed yet.

Before you start: Start with an existing Vanilla application using Vite. Run the commands from its root directory; this tutorial does not scaffold a new app.

Outcome: A visible star icon that you can resize and recolor with a single prop.

#### 1. Install the packages

The adapter renders SVGs. The Vite plugin finds literal icon names in your code and includes their artwork in your build.

Run these commands inside your application.

File: Terminal

```
bun add @icones/vanilla
bun add -d @icones/vite
```

Run these commands in your application directory. They require access to the @icones packages in your registry; if a package is unavailable, obtain a compatible release before continuing.

Check your result: Your app has both @icones/vanilla and @icones/vite in its dependencies.

#### 2. Connect the artwork

Add icones to your existing plugin list; keep your framework’s other plugins. Set dataDir to the directory containing your icon JSON files. This example assumes icons is inside the application root.

On the Icons page, find tabler:star, open its JSON tab and save the original JSON as icons/tabler/data/star.json in your application. Keep the collection’s license from the Licenses page with any artwork you use.

Update vite.config.ts, then restart your Vite development server so it reads the new plugin configuration.

File: vite.config.ts

```
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import { icones } from "@icones/vite"

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    // Keep your existing framework plugin here.
    icones({
      mode: "symbol",
      dataDir: "./icons",
      emitData: false,
    }),
  ],
})
```

File: project-layout.txt

```
your-app/
  icons/tabler/data/star.json
  vite.config.ts
```

Note: Use the original tuple JSON from the JSON tab, not SVG markup. Save other icons with the same <set>/data/<name>.json layout. Set fallbackToApi: false to prevent build-time requests for missing icons.

Check your result: The file icons/tabler/data/star.json exists in your application. dataDir points to ./icons, the folder containing tabler/, not to the JSON file itself.

- [Vite and API loading](/guide/loading)

#### 3. Display your first icon

Add this to index.html. Write the dedicated icones-icon tag and import @icones/vanilla/web-element once. The browser upgrades the tag and appends an SVG directly inside it, without Shadow DOM. Keep the icon in HTML.

Run your app with its normal development command and open the page. Verify the star is visible before continuing.

File: icon.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="24"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

Check your result: You see one 24px star. In the DOM it contains an SVG; no IconConfig or runtime API setup is required.

#### 4. Change one thing at a time

In the previous example, change size from 24 to 32. Once the star grows, add color to make it purple. Keep the name and loading setup unchanged.

This complete replacement example combines those two changes. Remove color to follow the surrounding text color again.

File: icon.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="32"
  color="#7712f7"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

Check your result: The same star is now 32px and purple. You changed its presentation, not its source JSON.

- [Next: color, sizing and stroke](/guide/vanilla/web/color)
- [Then: Web Components attributes and deferred rendering](/guide/vanilla/web/overview)
- [Later: share defaults with IconConfig](/guide/vanilla/web/icon-config)

#### If the icon does not appear

Check these in order before adding configuration. Shared defaults cannot fix a missing import, an incorrect path or missing artwork.

Reference section (optional).

- Check the terminal for a missing-package or missing-icon error.
- Confirm the icon’s name is exactly tabler:star, and dataDir contains tabler/data/star.json.
- Restart the development server after changing its configuration.
- Use a Vite-served page, not a file:// URL. Confirm the module script imports @icones/vanilla/web-element and the host uses icones-icon with name.
- Check that CSS is not hiding the SVG or giving it the same color as the background.
- Use a literal name for this lesson. Computed names need local data or a runtime loading setup; learn that after the first icon works.

chapters.title: Color
chapters.markdown:
### Web Components · Color

[Source](/guide/vanilla/web/color)

Let icons follow your text, or give a single icon its own color.

#### Inherit text color

Monochrome icons use currentColor. When color is omitted, the drawing follows the surrounding text color, so it fits naturally inside links, buttons and status messages.

File: icon.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  size="24"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

#### Set an explicit color

The color option accepts a CSS color. Use a hex value, a named color, or a design token such as var(--accent-color).

File: icon.html

```
<icones-icon
  name="tabler:star"
  color="#7712f7"
  size="24"
></icones-icon>

<script type="module">
  import "@icones/vanilla/web-element"
</script>
```

#### Color in Outline, Filled and Solid icons

The SVG color value does not replace every fill or stroke. It affects only paint values that use currentColor. The artwork decides whether that color appears on an outline or a filled area.

Outline, Filled and Solid describe the artwork, not color modes. Select the exact icon name to change styles; setting color or fill does not turn an outline drawing into its designed filled counterpart.

| Style | What changes with color |
| --- | --- |
| Outline | Usually colors strokes (stroke="currentColor") while fill="none" keeps the center empty. Example: tabler:star. |
| Filled | Usually colors the solid shape through fill="currentColor". Example: tabler:star-filled. It does not add a separate outline. |
| Solid | The same color behavior as Filled, with the collection’s own naming. Example: bootstrap:star-fill. |
